text:
morgan: heads-up, linux-integ is red on main after the 10:42 deploy, failing an e2e that hits the scheduler, looks like a timing/timeout regression
elaine: is this the flaky test we saw yesterday or something new?
morgan: new failure pattern — backend logs show repeated 'task acquisition timed out' in the scheduler worker. last green for the pipeline was 1819054321 (before the agent image bump)
sam: tagging @devops — we pushed an updated buildkite agent image in the last roll, could be related :thinking_face:
devops: saw a couple of agent updates. which job is failing?
morgan: job: integration/scheduler-compat, step `run-integ --mode=parallel`. Error snippet: ```ERROR scheduler.worker: failed to acquire task within 30s
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/scheduler/worker.py", line 132, in poll
    task = queue.get(timeout=30)
queue.Empty: 
```
leo: hmm queue.Empty with no other exception — could be network/connectivity to redis or the agent not mounting the right volume
elaine: I can reproduce locally with the image if someone posts the exact image tag
morgan: image tag is `redwood/agent:2026-03-15-abc123` (pushed 2026-03-15T10:30)
ci-bot: pipeline: main/linux-integ #482 failed (https://ci.redwood.dev/pipelines/482) — rerun triggered by @morgan
sam: before bisecting the commit range, can we quickly revert the agent image in the pipeline to the previous tag `redwood/agent:2026-03-14-ff9b2` to confirm?
devops: I can flip the image in the staging pipeline env var and trigger a rerun in ~5m if you want
elaine: +1, quick revert will tell us if the image is culprit or something in the repo
morgan: sounds good, if revert fixes it we can do a git bisect across the deploys to narrow down which change in the image caused it
leo: if revert doesn't fix, next step is bisection across recent commits on main. last green commit hash (from CI history) 8f3a7c2 — need volunteers to run the bisect since it will require reproducing the integ job locally a few times
sam: I can kick off a bisect run later today — what command do you want me to use?
morgan: start with `git bisect start HEAD 8f3a7c2` then for each bad/good build we use our integ runner script: `scripts/run_integ.sh --image local` — mark good/bad based on the same integration step failing
sam: ok. will also collect perf counters and scheduler logs each step and post back. ETA ~3 hours
sre-bot: reminder: if you need to run >5 bisection builds on CI, open a capacity request with eng-infra to avoid job throttling
morgan: noted. @devops can you do the image flip now?
devops: doing it now — changing env var and starting rerun. I'll post the rerun link when it starts
(2m later)
devops: rerun started: https://ci.redwood.dev/pipelines/483
elaine: watching the logs. stepping through setup...
(6m later)
elaine: looks like the rerun with previous image passed the failing step :tada:
morgan: excellent — that points at the agent image. thanks @devops and @elaine
leo: next: coordinate with infra team that built the image to roll back the bad change and also run a delta diff on the agent config (systemd, ulimits, network args)
devops: pinging infra-image-team. also opening a revert MR for the pipeline env so we can keep main green while we investigate
sam: I'll still run a local bisect against the image builds (if infra can give me the image build artifacts/tags) to find which image layer introduced the change
morgan: perfect. logging action items: 1) devops revert pipeline image (in flight) 2) infra-image-team to diff agent image layers 3) sam to bisect image builds and report back 4) if bisect points to code in our repo, we escalate to eng leads
elaine: adding this thread to the incident channel for visibility :point_up:
morgan: thanks all, will update here when sam has bisect results or infra posts a root cause
(reacts: :thumbsup: from leo, :rocket: from devops)
